title: The Bigger Picture — Daily AI Analysis
paragraphs: A deeper look at today's Bigger Picture card: what is moving the market, and what to watch. The Full Report carries the full analysis.

What moves the market today. Fact: Reuters reports that the cost of insuring against defaults by technology companies hit record highs on Thursday, led by CoreWeave, the data centre operator, whose five-year contract passed 1,100 basis points, a level Reuters says implies a 64 percent chance of default within five years, against about 30 percent a year ago. Fact: Business Insider reports that the largest chip and memory companies have lost more than 1 trillion dollars of market value this week, and the Associated Press reports that US indexes still rose on Thursday on company profits while South Korea's Kospi fell 7.6 percent.

Fact: Fortune reports that TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, posted a record quarterly net profit of about 24 billion dollars, up 69 percent, and said demand is far above what it can supply, while C.C. Wei, its chairman and chief executive, called the company prudent about 2027. Fact: Reuters reports, citing four people familiar with the matter, that some investors are weighing a valuation of about 1.5 trillion dollars for Anthropic's planned stock market listing, down from roughly 2 trillion, after revenue figures that Anthropic has not confirmed.

Our view: the AI build is not short of demand; it is being repriced on the cost of money. The supplier at the bottom posted a record and the most indebted borrower at the top paid a record for insurance on the same day, and the gap between those two prices is where the next weeks will be decided. Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, which owns about a tenth of CoreWeave, said it needs no rescue; the market priced the opposite.

What to watch and follow. 1. Wednesday 21 October: Meta's results, the first of the four biggest AI spenders to say whether its 2027 plan holds (Meta's own notice, checked earlier this week); a trimmed plan would be the first crack on the demand side. 2. 27 to 29 October: SK hynix's results (its own filing names 28 October, Seoul time), the Federal Reserve's decision on 28 October (its own calendar), and the results of Alphabet, Microsoft and Intel (Intel's own notice names 29 October). 3. CoreWeave's default insurance day by day: a new bond priced well below 14 percent would end the scare, a cancelled customer contract would deepen it. 4. Anthropic's answer to Mark Levine, New York City's comptroller, who asked it to pause its listing until it sets out audits, and any public filing with a price range.

Unknowns. Whether Anthropic's 16.8 billion dollars of quarterly revenue is counted before or after its cloud partners' share; what the Financial Times found behind its report of investors selling data centre bonds; and whether CoreWeave's cost of capital is falling while its bonds yield 14 to 16 percent. This is analysis of the news, not financial advice or an investment recommendation.
